title: Evening Brief — Fri 27 Nov

stories.board: Eisenkot says new Israeli government within 8 days
stories.headline: Eisenkot races the clock to form Israel's next government
stories.what: Gadi Eisenkot has 8 days left to build a coalition (a team of parties with a majority). He says he will not ask for more time. Yair Golan's Democrats signed a deal to join him, but Naftali Bennett has not yet.
stories.why: Whoever forms the government becomes Israel's next leader.
stories.sides: Eisenkot accuses Likud of stalling the talks; Netanyahu is reportedly weighing a rotation (taking turns as prime minister), with Netanyahu going second.

stories.board: Pakistan and Turkey back Saudis against Houthis
stories.headline: Pakistan and Turkey promise to help Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
stories.what: Leaders from the three countries met in Pakistan under their Mecca defense pact (a promise to protect each other). They condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Houthis, a rebel group in Yemen backed by Iran. Turkey finished approving the pact on Friday.
stories.why: Two big military powers are now formally tied to Saudi Arabia's safety, which could change the balance in the Middle East.
stories.sides: No major disagreement. Pakistan and Turkey say the pact is only for defense, and Turkey says it will not send troops to fight in Yemen.

stories.board: Nine Ukrainian kids home with Melania Trump's help
stories.headline: Nine Ukrainian children returned from Russia with help from Melania Trump
stories.what: Nine children taken to Russia or Russian-held land went back to their families in Ukraine. President Zelensky said Melania Trump helped mediate (talk between both sides to reach a deal).
stories.why: Ukraine says thousands of its children were taken during the war, so every return matters.
stories.sides: No major disagreement on the facts; right-leaning outlets stress her quiet work and say she gets little credit for it.

stories.board: Freedom founder fights Quebecor's $31B Telus bid
stories.headline: Fight grows over Quebecor's $31 billion offer to buy Telus
stories.what: Quebecor, which owns Freedom Mobile, offered about $31 billion to buy Telus. Freedom's founder, Anthony Lacavera, called the deal a disaster and wants to buy Freedom back to keep it separate.
stories.why: If the deal goes through, Canada would have three big phone companies instead of four, and experts warn bills could go up.
stories.sides: Not a left-right split: Quebecor wants to grow bigger, while consumer groups and Lacavera worry about less competition. Regulators (government watchdogs) are watching.

quick_hits: US stocks closed higher in the short Black Friday session; the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 fund rose about 2.7 percent.
Brazil's markets jumped after President Lula picked banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco as finance minister (the person in charge of the country's money).
Hamas says the last surviving son of its leader Khalil al-Hayya lived through an Israeli airstrike in Gaza; Israel's army had no comment (Ynetnews).
big_picture: Deals ruled the day: a coalition race in Israel, a defense pact in the Middle East, and a phone mega-merger fight in Canada.
